detailed_review.score_reasoning: Baseline 10 - (F1 2 + F2 1 + F3 0.5 + F4 0.5) = 6. F1 is a 2 because the landing rules at wiki/page-types.md:91-92 are stated flatly and violated twice in one section, and because the page that owns the duplicated convention is linked in that same section. F2 is a 1 because a noun heading where the type asks for a gerund is a scanability defect rather than a blocker, and because the 'pages' imprecision misleads a reader only mildly: entry 1 still tells them exactly where the steps will land. F3 and F4 are 0.5 each, low-consequence shape and sentence-logic nits, and both were fixable in place. After the pass, F3 and F4 are cleared and F1 and F2 remain open by design, giving 10 - 3 = 7. Delta +1. Both grades are absolute readings of the page, so the +1 is a measured difference rather than credit awarded for effort. Two things are deliberately not in this math. Anything scripts/lint_wiki.py owns is out of scope, and I confirmed its ownership by reading it at lines 216, 356-386 rather than inferring it. And the T12 edit under review is itself sound: I re-verified every assertion in entry 1 against source and the tracker and found no stale claim, so the delivered work contributes nothing to the penalty.
detailed_review.what_worked: The delivered T12 edit is correct, which is the main thing to report, and I verified it independently rather than accepting the author's account. crates/hearth-probe/dictionary.yaml:102 reads `cpp_platforms: [macos, windows]` and desktop-client/src-tauri/src/provision.rs:476-479 returns before the venv, torch and engine chain with 'engine ships with Hearth', so the removed CUDA voice claim was genuinely false and is genuinely gone. tasks/docs/tracker.md:1394-1396 makes the deliverable a `### Windows` procedure inside wiki/installing.md rather than a separate page, which is what the entry now says. wiki/installing.md:69-89 does already state the Windows requirements, as the entry claims. tasks/docs/tracker.md:1386 and 1391-1392 support the blocker clause. wiki/clients/windows.md:245-246 states its scope in the same terms the entry uses for it. The link to install-macos.md is gone, which is the precondition T16 needed from this page. On top of that, F3 gives the first section the orienting sentence its type requires and its neighbour already had, and F4 straightens the causal chain in the one sentence this task existed to deliver, so a reader now reads the blocker and the standard in the order they actually relate.
detailed_review.what_holds_score_down: Two open findings, both structural, both pre-existing and outside the corrections task's scope. F1 is the larger by some distance. ## Material that never publishes spends four of its six sentences teaching a documentation contributor how to cite a raw/ source and what the linter rejects, on a page whose type forbids anything a reader can act on, and then links wiki/developing.md, which is where that material already lives. A reader who came to find out what is missing does not leave within one screen, which is the one thing wiki/page-types.md:69-70 asks of a landing page. F2 is smaller and partly acknowledged already: both headings are noun labels where the corpus model wiki/_index.md uses gerunds in all six of its sections, and 'Pages' now overstates a list holding one missing section and one missing page. Neither was fixed here, and neither should have been by this stage: F1 is a reshape, and F2 the dispatch explicitly reserved. Worth being plain that the page is not in bad shape. It is short, its every factual claim survived checking against source, and its links all resolve and all say something true about their destinations. The 7 is a type-conformance grade, not a trustworthiness one.
